blocks.overview: Keystone RV Company appeals a Tax Court decision dismissing its motion and granting the respondent's motion to amend pleadings in a GST/HST reassessment dispute. The case concerns the correctness of reassessments and procedural motions under the Excise Tax Act. The Federal Court of Appeal dismissed Keystone's appeal with costs.

blocks.issue: Should Keystone's Rule 170.1 motion for judgment based on the Minister's concession be granted?
blocks.court_conclusion: No palpable and overriding error in rejecting Keystone's Rule 170.1 motion; material disputes remain requiring trial.

positions.text: Only issue is correct GST/HST adjustment; Minister admitted reassessments incorrect, so Rule 170.1 motion must be granted.
No palpable and overriding error in rejecting Rule 170.1 motion; disputes remain requiring trial; Rule 170.1 requires no controversy on facts or legal issues.
Minister's concession did not eliminate controversy; assumptions about underreporting and invalid credits remain disputed.

blocks.issue: Was the Tax Court's granting of the respondent's Rule 54 motion to amend its Reply appropriate?
blocks.court_conclusion: No reviewable error in granting Rule 54 motion; amendment clarifies issues and serves justice; Minister's concession is not an appeal.

positions.text: Respondent's Rule 54 motion was an abusive attempt to appeal the Minister's assessment.
No error in granting Rule 54 motion; broad amendment rights apply; amendment clarifies issues and causes no injustice; Minister's concession not an appeal.
Motions judge found no factual foundation for improper conduct allegations; Rule 170.1 motion not proper vehicle for such allegations.

blocks.issue: Did the Tax Court err in awarding costs to the respondent?
blocks.court_conclusion: No error in costs awards; Keystone was satisfied with costs award in Rule 54 motion.

positions.text: No error in costs awards; Keystone was satisfied with costs award in Rule 54 motion.

propositions.text: Keystone RV Company is the appellant appealing an interlocutory Tax Court decision dated December 15, 2023.
The Tax Court dismissed Keystone's Rule 170.1 motion and granted the respondent's Rule 54 motion to amend its Reply.
The Tax Court awarded costs to the respondent on both motions.

paragraphs.summary: The court states Keystone appeals a December 15, 2023 Tax Court decision dismissing its Rule 170.1 motion, granting respondent's Rule 54 motion, and awarding costs to respondent.

propositions.text: Keystone appeals CRA reassessments dated February 21, 2018 under the Excise Tax Act for seven monthly GST/HST periods in 2014.
The reassessments imposed an additional net GST/HST of $24,695,247.20 on Keystone.

paragraphs.summary: The court explains Keystone appeals CRA reassessments imposing over $24 million GST/HST for seven 2014 reporting periods.

propositions.text: Respondent conceded in a November 14, 2022 letter that the correct net GST/HST adjustment is $4,203,799.29.
Keystone relied on this concession to bring a Rule 170.1 motion arguing the only issue is the correct net GST/HST adjustment and the Minister admitted the reassessments were incorrect.

paragraphs.summary: The court states respondent conceded a lower GST/HST adjustment in November 2022, and Keystone moved under Rule 170.1 relying on this admission.

propositions.text: Respondent filed a Rule 54 motion to amend its Reply consistent with the November 14, 2022 letter, including a proposed amended Reply as Schedule A.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes respondent filed a Rule 54 motion to amend its Reply consistent with the November 2022 concession.

propositions.text: Standard of review is palpable and overriding error for fact and mixed fact-law questions, correctness for law questions, citing Housen v. Nikolaisen.
An error is palpable if obvious or plainly seen, and overriding if it affects the result, citing Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce v. Canada.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the standard of review is palpable and overriding error for facts, correctness for law, defining palpable and overriding errors.

propositions.text: The court finds no error of law or palpable and overriding error in the Tax Court's rejection of Keystone's Rule 170.1 motion.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds no legal or palpable overriding error in the Tax Court's rejection of Keystone's Rule 170.1 motion.

propositions.text: Rule 170.1 allows a party to apply for judgment at any stage based on admissions in pleadings, documents, or examination of a party.

paragraphs.summary: The court explains Rule 170.1 permits judgment applications based on admissions in pleadings or examinations at any stage.

propositions.text: Tax Court correctly identified Rule 170.1 requires no controversy on facts or fairly arguable legal issues to grant judgment, citing Georgeson and Iris Technologies.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Tax Court correctly applied the principle that Rule 170.1 requires no factual or legal controversy to grant judgment.

propositions.text: Keystone argues the only issue is correctness of reassessments and the Minister admitted reassessments are incorrect, so Rule 170.1 motion must be granted.

paragraphs.summary: Keystone argues only the reassessment correctness is at issue and the Minister's admission requires granting its Rule 170.1 motion.

propositions.text: The court disagrees and finds no palpable and overriding error in the Tax Court's application of Georgeson to Keystone's Rule 170.1 motion.

paragraphs.summary: The court disagrees with Keystone and finds no palpable overriding error in the Tax Court's application of the Georgeson test.

propositions.text: Tax Court found Minister's November 2022 concession did not eliminate controversy; assumptions about underreporting and invalid credits remain disputed.
The court agrees there remain clear, material disputes requiring trial as few facts are established and no discoveries held, citing Iris FCA.

paragraphs.summary: The court agrees with the Tax Court that material disputes remain despite the Minister's concession, requiring trial.

propositions.text: Keystone argues the November 14 letter and amended Reply show the Minister abandoned original assumptions and conceded all matters, entitling Keystone to judgment under Rule 170.1.

paragraphs.summary: Keystone argues the Minister abandoned original assumptions and conceded all matters, entitling Keystone to judgment under Rule 170.1.

propositions.text: Keystone did not raise the 'matters' argument in its Rule 170.1 motion or before the motions judge, so cannot now claim error for failure to consider it.
Keystone also did not assert error in the notice of appeal or memorandum regarding the motions judge's focus, so the court need not address this argument on appeal.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Keystone did not raise the 'matters' argument below or on appeal, so the court need not address it now.

propositions.text: The court finds Keystone's argument unpersuasive and notes no authority limits Georgeson to specific matters or assumptions in reassessments.
Subsections 298(6.1)-(6.3) of the Act allow the Minister to advance alternative bases or arguments supporting assessments, not limited to specific matters.

paragraphs.summary: The court rejects Keystone's argument, noting the Act allows the Minister to advance alternative bases or arguments supporting assessments.

propositions.text: Keystone submits the Tax Court failed to consider evidence of alleged improper and abusive CRA conduct fabricating reassessment facts.

paragraphs.summary: Keystone submits the Tax Court failed to consider evidence of alleged improper and abusive CRA conduct fabricating reassessment facts.

propositions.text: Motions judge found no factual foundation to assess improper conduct allegations due to inadequate time and that Rule 170.1 motion was not the proper vehicle for such allegations.
The court agrees the Rule 170.1 motion concerned only whether the net GST/HST amount remains disputed.

paragraphs.summary: The court agrees the motions judge properly declined to assess improper conduct allegations in the Rule 170.1 motion focused on net GST/HST dispute.

propositions.text: Keystone argues the respondent's Rule 54 motion was an abusive attempt to appeal the Minister's assessment, citing Continental Bank of Canada v. Canada.

paragraphs.summary: Keystone argues the respondent's Rule 54 motion was an abusive attempt to appeal the Minister's assessment.

propositions.text: The court disagrees and finds no reviewable error in granting the respondent's Rule 54 motion, noting broad amendment rights and application of subsections 298(3), (6.1)-(6.3).
The amended Reply clarifies real issues, causes no injustice, and serves justice interests, citing Pomeroy.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds no error in granting respondent's Rule 54 motion, as the amended Reply clarifies issues and serves justice.

propositions.text: The Minister's concession reducing the assessed amount is not an appeal of the assessment, citing Beaulieu v. The Queen.
TPine Leasing confirms the Minister cannot appeal an assessment but allows alternative bases under different legislation; motions judge's reasoning aligns with TPine.
Keystone has not shown palpable and overriding error in the motions judge's analysis of the Rule 54 motion.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Minister's concession is not an appeal, aligns with TPine, and Keystone shows no error in the Rule 54 motion analysis.

propositions.text: The court finds no error in the Tax Court's awards of costs and notes Keystone was satisfied with the costs award in the Rule 54 motion.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds no error in the Tax Court's costs awards and notes Keystone's satisfaction with the Rule 54 motion costs award.

propositions.text: Dismiss the appeal with costs.

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the appeal with costs.
